intro1: Ahoy! I'm Pip. This is Foul Weather, a game built on NEAR. Let me show you how it works.
intro2: You run a little shop in a harbor. Sailors are scared of storms, so they pay you to protect their ships.
card: Here comes a captain. Each one is a real character, with a wallet of their own.
earn: The green number is what they pay you, right now.
lose: The red number is what you pay if the ship sinks. Ouch!
meter: This meter shows if the deal is good. Green is great. Red means say no.
yes: This one is in the green, so let's tap yes!
sailed: The ship sets sail, and the coins are ours! See the gold ring on the map? That's our ship.
home: She made it! Tap the star to collect it. Stars let you decorate your harbor, and every level teaches you a new trick.
lost: Oh no, a shipwreck! That's the risk. A good shop chooses its ships carefully.
waiting: While the ship sails, everything keeps moving by itself. Prices, fees and captains all change.
spiral1: Now for the big one. Every shop in town has paid another shop to help with its risk. Nobody can see the whole chain. And a huge storm is coming.
fall: One shop can't pay. So the shop that was counting on it can't pay either. They fall like dominoes.
gone1: One storm, and those shops are gone. Only the storm was planned. Who fell, and in what order, came from the game's real rules.
gone2: Real insurance markets have failed this way. Here, it's a game you can learn from.
live1: That was practice, running right here in the browser. Now let's go online. One tap, and the same game opens on NEAR. There's no wallet and no password. An account is being made for us right now.
live2: We're in. This town is shared with real players, and there's no game server. One NEAR contract holds the rules and all the coins. The captains' wallets have no keys, so only the rules can move their money.
live3: I just tapped yes, and it happened on the blockchain, with no popup. There's the receipt, under Last action.
live4: Each sea route follows a real price from NEAR Intents, so real markets make the water rough or calm, all by themselves.
end: That's Foul Weather. You don't trade the goods. You carry the risk. Now it's your turn!
